goal: The worker establishes a deterministic git identity on every provisioned worktree so an in-sandbox git commit succeeds with no global or system git identity present.

relevant: packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- GitWorktreeSubmitter.prepare_sandbox and its _add_worktree/_discard_and_recreate helpers (worktree provisioning); add the identity step on every freshly provisioned worktree here
packages/flywheel-worktree/tests/test_worker.py -- the existing worktree suite (prepare/submit/run_once); keep every test green
.flywheel/specs/00027-FEATURE-worktree-commit-integrity.md -- criteria 1, 2 and D-3 (identity reachable WITHOUT a global/system gitconfig); Decomposition Layer A
constraints: The committer/author name and email must be fixed module-level constants in worker.py (one named constant each), identical across every worktree this worker provisions in a repo -- not random, UUID, timestamp, or per-run derived (criterion 2).

The identity must be reachable by a plain `git commit` run inside the worktree under a scrubbed environment (empty HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1) -- i.e. it must live on a surface the in-worktree git process reads with no ambient config, such as worktree-local `git config user.name/user.email`. An identity injected only into the worker's own subprocess environment (GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* on the worker process) is NOT seen by the agent's separate in-sandbox commit and will fail criterion 1.

Apply the identity on every freshly created worktree path in prepare_sandbox (the brand-new -b branch path, the recreate-on-surviving-branch path, and the discard-and-recreate path); a reused parked worktree already carries its config.
The worker still authors no commit on the base/operator branch -- this task only makes the AGENT's in-sandbox commit able to succeed; it does NOT add git add/git commit to the worker (D-1).
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not modify files under packages/flywheel-worktree/tests/ or under .flywheel/holdout/00027-worktree-commit-integrity/ (the held-out grading surface); do not weaken or delete existing assertions.
Do not touch the dirty-tree-vs-no-op classification at the head of _submit (worker.py:439-457) -- that is the next task.
Do not touch _ff_merge, _phase_base, base resolution, rebase/re-verify, or the divergent-base park -- those are spec 00026's TAIL.
Do not add a flywheel.toml config key for the identity; the constants are fixed in code (no [submit]/[sandbox] scaffolding).
edge_cases: A per-worktree random/UUID/timestamp identity would pass 'a commit exists' but FAIL the cross-worktree byte-equality assertion -- the identity must be constant across two independently provisioned worktrees.
Setting identity only in the test repo's own config (the path the scrubbed environment removes) must not be how the commit succeeds -- the worker must establish it itself.
GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 plus empty HOME means neither system nor global config resolves; only worktree/repo-local config or per-call -c overrides reach the in-worktree commit.
notes: Held-out graders run `uv run pytest .flywheel/holdout/00027-worktree-commit-integrity/ -k <keyword>`; those tests are authored out-of-band by the fw-verify step (the implementing agent does not write them). The scrubbed-identity environment (empty HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1) is a single shared fixture there, exercised by criteria 1, 2 and 6. The holdout path is outside the four pytest testpaths, so a bare `uv run pytest` never collects it; the grader passes the path explicitly.
